Why this alignment: The standard lists four purposes for using texts: build knowledge, develop skills, make informed decisions, and share information and ideas. These are an object list with the same verb ("use texts to..."), so any one met would satisfy the clause. Students clearly use texts (read-aloud, photos, videos) to build knowledge about the sun, moon, and stars, and they share information and ideas based on those texts. Since this is an object list with the same verb, meeting any one purpose satisfies the standard. However, re-reading the skill_clauses and the standard more carefully — the standard says "build knowledge, develop skills, make informed decisions, and share information and ideas" — these could be read as interchangeable targets under the same verb "make use of texts to." Why this alignment: Students engage in dialogue with peers during the Picture Tea Party and Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocols. They answer questions posed by the teacher and share observations. They also generate their own wonderings using the "I wonder" sentence frame, which they share with partners during dialogue. However, the "ask" component is somewhat indirect — students share wonderings rather than directly asking questions of their audience/partner. The "I wonder" frame shared during the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocol does constitute student-generated questions shared during dialogue, but the dialogic exchange is more about sharing notices and wonders than a true back-and-forth of asking and answering questions between students. Additionally, the scaffold step for ELLs explicitly models questions like "Can you please repeat what you said?" but this is scaffold-only. On balance, the "ask" clause is met but thinly — students do generate and share wonder-questions with partners. All three clauses appear met, warranting full. Let me reconsider: students share "I wonder" statements with partners during the protocol, which counts as asking questions during dialogue. Students answer teacher questions. Students engage in dialogue. All clauses are met in core steps.
